releases.notes:
Rebranded to Splyt — new name, new icon. Same app, same data, nothing you
need to do.

Splyt opens with a new animation — the wordmark splits down the middle and
pulls back to your Home.

Your Apple Watch opens on a microphone. Tap it, say "basketball", "start my
plan", "rest day" — it counts down 3-2-1 and starts.

Say your split out loud and Splyt builds it. It reads gym shorthand, times
said loosely — "half four", "after work" — and a rambling take where the
days and times arrive in any order.

The watch rest screen is redesigned: a ring counting down, your heart rate,
−30s / +30s in the corners. Swipe right to see your next set, left for your
music.

Fix sets by voice. "I started with 10 pounds and then did 30 for the rest"
corrects the sets you already logged instead of piling more underneath them.

A personal record is a moment now. The rest bar opens into a card showing
how far you beat your best, and the set keeps the trophy.

Send your week to your trainer. The Weekly Recap exports your training day
by day, PRs, weight, steps, sleep and habits — as a PDF, or a private link
that opens in any browser. You pick what goes in it.

The training calendar is redrawn — one row a day, today raised with its
sessions already open — and the home screen widget matches it. Copy a day
you've already planned and it lands with its times.

Share a workout with anyone. Your summary opens as a web page, so friends
without Splyt can see what you did — and tapping a splyt.fit link opens it
straight in the app.

Browse the whole exercise library from Stats without starting a workout.
Search it, filter by body part, tap any record to open that exercise.

Closing your Splyt ring flashes and glows. Your watch counts rows and other
horizontal pulls.

A phone you've used before opens on "Welcome back" — one tap to continue.

Plus a faster way to start a workout, and a long list of fixes.

Start just one activity from a planned day and you get that activity — not the day's main workout loaded into it.

Discard a workout and it stays discarded. It no longer reappears as a finished, empty session or push your plan on to the next thing.

Your character's picture no longer sticks as a black square after signing out and back in.

Tap a friend's name in your plan to see what they trained.

Building a core workout now offers core movements and asks about core.

Removing a day's first activity renames the day to match what's left.

Big new things

The Vessel — swipe right in any live activity, a glass fills as you go against last time / typical / best. Lifts race weight moved, not the clock.
Friends tab rebuilt — empty state leads with the founders (tap to read their story and numbers), and a friend's friends now list on their profile, one tap from Add.
Use these sets — paste a past session's sets onto the movement you're on.
OTA updates — screen-only changes can now reach users without an App Store trip.
Competitions got a real cleanup

Sleep races count the nights you didn't log — logging eight nights used to lose to someone who logged two.
Forfeit races name who actually came last and what they owe; results land 9 PM.
No more "someone passed you" the morning after a race ended.
Timed core work no longer counts as weight lifted (a 60s plank was adding 600 lb).
Friend-facing fixes

Your lifts show their real names on a friend's screen instead of "Traditional Strength Training".
Opening one activity in a friend's workout no longer offers Edit, Share or Scan.
Everyone's called by their chosen display name, not their sign-up first name.
Plus — free-tier group locks, Siri on a locked phone, watch auto-rep, photo permissions, live Graph redraw, workout settings mid-session, pressable This Week bars.

What I did today specifically: the sleep-race scoring (four copies of the same wrong rule), the display-name sweep across six notification paths, the friend-workout naming + owner-gating, and the split-view fixes. Plus corrected your Best Sleep race — it now reads 6.73 to 1.70 in your favour.

The live workout, redesigned. Your workout's name and clock sit at the top with Finish and a menu beside them, every movement is its own card, and a floating pill holds the mic and add. While you rest it shows how long is left — drag it sideways to change the rest, tap it for fifteen more seconds.

Create your own character. Describe anything — a purple bear, a lightbulb, your dog — or start from a photo. Make yourself from a selfie and a full-length shot, in the clothes you're wearing or ones you describe. Animated or fully realistic, and private to you.

The character library. Everything anyone has made and shared, free for everyone to use.

Splits have a home. Open the training calendar and tap the grid to pick a proven split sorted by how many days a week you train, build one by hand, or drag a day to move everything on it. Splits can roll — four days on, one off — so your week no longer has to be seven days long.

Say your split. Tap the mic and describe your week — "push, pull, legs, rest, repeat, everything at 3 PM" — and it lands as your week, days and times in place.

Competition maps move like maps. Pinch to zoom on the spot under your fingers, twist to turn, drag with two fingers to tilt. When a race ends, see how far your steps would have taken you on a real map, with everyone on the line and an award for each person that's true of their week.

Race chat. A message from the group buzzes your phone; tap a photo to see it full screen, zoom, save or share.

On your watch: Activity rings pick up your ring theme's gradient instead of three flat colours, supersets go round by round, and reps are counted on more movements.

Dozens of fixes, including workouts that kept counting after you left, splits that read 0% however much you trained, and the rest chime arriving late.

Share any saved workout as a link. Whoever opens it sees every set, weight and rep, and can save it to their own library.

Plan a split by picking the shape of your week — full body, upper/lower, push/pull/legs and more, drawn day by day with the muscles each one trains.

Your Apple Watch now counts reps on lat pulldowns and straight-arm pulldowns.

Competitions: accept or decline an invite right on the map, see when someone leaves a race, and report or block in chat.

Workouts end when you end them. The last activity of a session could keep counting long after you'd left.

Faster set logging during a workout, and your week now starts on the day you chose — habits, profile and streaks included.

Plus a long list of smaller fixes across notifications, recaps and the watch.

- Competitions you can watch — your race runs in a road, a gym or a pool, with a character you pick.
- A race that hasn't started opens on its own fight card, and you can see who's training right now.
- Bug fixes
Recaps now include your training calendar, and shared workouts preview properly. Plus fixes across sign-in, habits, supersets and rest timers.

Your ring is actually yours — turn pillars off or set your own activity rule
Sharing — Share Day for your whole day
Planning — editing a planned day now edits the day itself, with the full builder, and you can move or cancel sessions, including recurrences.
Workouts — reorder mid-workout with supersets moving as one block, bodyweight lifts counting toward volume, and the watch honouring your real rest times.

Everything since our last release — this is the biggest update Tempo has ever shipped.

Your watch counts your reps.
Apple Watch now counts reps for you on bench press, shoulder press, curls, squats, triceps work, and chest flyes. A live count appears mid-set on your wrist, and your phone takes over the whole screen with a count you can read from across the room. Keep it with a tap, or slide to correct it.

Tempo talks to your gym's machines.
No Bluetooth machine? Snap a photo of the console and Tempo reads your metrics straight into the workout.

Lifting got serious.
Supersets, giant sets, drop sets, and warm-up and failure sets are now first-class — in your live workout and baked into your templates. A new in-workout keyboard built for lifting keeps the system keyboard out of your way. Tap the bar icon on any barbell lift to see exactly which plates to load. Log reps in reserve with the Effort slider. Set per-set reps for pyramids and dropsets.

Outdoor tracking without a watch.
Start an outdoor run, walk, ride, or hike with just your phone and watch your distance, pace, and route map update live. Your route saves to your summary and to anything you share — including a card built for your Instagram Story.

Your day, in one ring.
The Tempo ring blends workouts, sleep, and habits into a single daily target, no Apple Watch required. Set your Move, Exercise, and Stand goals right inside Tempo, pick from dozens of ring colorways, and put your ring on your lock screen, home screen, or watch face.

A coach that does more.
Tempo AI is now one continuous, searchable conversation. It builds real programs with warm-ups, top sets, and supersets, edits your existing split when you ask, searches the web for what's current, and sets goals from a plain sentence like "box 5 times a week." Every plan shows you a Confirm card first — nothing lands on your calendar until you tap it. New voices and vibes too, from Calm to Drill Sergeant.

Compete, and see how everyone's doing.
Go head-to-head or as a group on workouts, volume, minutes, steps, sleep, or bedtime — all tracked automatically. Past competitions live on their own screen with each winner front and center. The Tempo Community brings a weekly challenge, a PR spotlight, and a recap of how the whole community trained.

Recovery counts now.
Sauna, cold plunge, ice bath, steam room, and massage sessions show up on your training calendar and in your stats as recovery, not training.

Stats worth opening.
Volume by body part, daily strain, training times, steps history, sleep stages, weight trends, and a weekly plain-language recap of the week you actually had.

Bring your training with you.
Import a workout from a pasted note, a photo, a CSV, a Google Sheet, or a link to a TikTok, Instagram, or YouTube video. Workouts from GymKit treadmills, Apple Fitness, Strava, and Nike Run Club sync into your history automatically.

Progress Photos (Pro).
Private, encrypted progress photos with weekly reminders — and an optional AI read on your physique with annotated callouts.

Plus a lot more.
Animated demos and step-by-step instructions on every exercise. Folders for saved workouts, shareable with friends. Missed workouts that stay on your record. Finish a workout with no signal and it saves the moment you reconnect. Demo mode so you can try Tempo before signing up. Report and block controls, and full account deletion from inside the app.
